questions.question: The ratio of the walking speeds of A and B is 3 : 5. If B takes 18 minutes to cover a certain distance, how much time will A take to cover the same distance?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of speeds of A and B = 3 : 5

Since distance is constant, the ratio of time taken is inversely proportional to the speed.

Ratio of time of A and B = 5 : 3

Time taken by B (3 parts) = 18 min

Time taken by A (5 parts) = (18 ÷ 3) × 5 = 30 min

**∴ The correct answer is 30 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of walking speeds of A and B = 3 : 5

Time taken by B = 18 min

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

 Distance = Speed × Time
 
 A :
 Speed = 3v
 Time = T min
 
 B :
 Speed = 5v
 Time = 18 min
 

 Distance is Constant

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the speed of A be 3v and the speed of B be 5v.

⇒ Let the time taken by A be T.

⇒ Since both cover the same distance, Distance by A = Distance by B

⇒ Speed of A × Time of A = Speed of B × Time of B

⇒ 3v × T = 5v × 18

⇒ 3 × T = 90

⇒ T = 90 ÷ 3

⇒ T = 30 min

**∴ The correct answer is 30 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportionality

When the distance is constant, speed and time are inversely proportional. Thus, S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂.

Average Speed

If two equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, then the Average Speed over the entire journey = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

If two bodies move in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂. If they move in the same direction, relative speed = |S₁ − S₂|.
</p

questions.question: Ketan sold 151 chairs and had a gain equal to the selling price of 51 chairs. What is his profit percentage?
questions.solution:
* __Shortcut Trick__

Let SP of 1 chair = 1 unit.

SP of 151 chairs = 151 units, and Gain = 51 units.

CP = Total SP − Gain = 151 − 51 = 100 units.

Profit % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100 = (51 ÷ 100) × 100 = 51%.

**∴ The correct answer is 51%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total chairs sold = 151

Gain = Selling Price of 51 chairs

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = Selling Price (SP) − Profit

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 

 Total Selling Price = 151 units
 
 
 
 
 Cost Price = 100
 Profit = 51

 Profit % = (51 ÷ 100) × 100 = 51%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let SP of 1 chair = 1 unit.

⇒ Total SP (151 chairs) = 151 units

⇒ Profit (SP of 51 chairs) = 51 units

⇒ CP = SP − Profit = 151 − 51 = 100 units

⇒ Profit % = (51 ÷ 100) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 51%

**∴ The correct answer is 51%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss in terms of Selling Price

If loss equals the SP of x* items when selling *y* items, then CP = SP of (*y* + *x*) items. Loss % = [*x* ÷ (*y* + *x*)] × 100.

Gain in terms of Cost Price

If gain equals the CP of *x* items when selling *y* items, then CP is equivalent to *y* items. Profit % = (*x* ÷ *y*) × 100.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

If a dealer sells goods at CP but uses false weight, Profit % = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100.
</p

questions.question: Chetan travels from City A to City B. If Chetan drives his car at (3)/(4) of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 33 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Chetan would have taken to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed ratio (Normal : New) = 4 : 3

Since distance is constant, Time ratio (Normal : New) = 3 : 4

Difference in time ratio parts = 4 − 3 = 1 part.

Given 1 part = 33 minutes.

Normal time (3 parts) = 33 × 3 = 99 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 99 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Speed = 3/4 S, Time = T + 33

**Given:**

New Speed = 3/4 of Normal Speed

Delay time = 33 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

Let the normal speed be S and the normal time taken be T.

⇒ Distance D = S × T

In the second case, New Speed = 3S/4

⇒ New Time taken = Distance ÷ New Speed

⇒ New Time = D ÷ (3S/4) = 4D / 3S

Substitute D = S × T into the new time equation:

⇒ New Time = 4 × (S × T) / 3S = 4T/3

The difference between the new time and normal time is given as 33 minutes.

⇒ (4T/3) − T = 33

⇒ (4T − 3T) / 3 = 33

⇒ T/3 = 33

⇒ T = 33 × 3 = 99 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 99 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion of Speed and Time

When the distance covered is constant, Speed and Time are inversely proportional to each other. S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂.

Average Speed

Average Speed is the ratio of Total Distance to Total Time. If equal distance is covered at speeds A and B, then Average Speed = (2 × A × B) / (A + B).

Relative Speed

For two bodies moving in opposite directions, the relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). If moving in the same direction, relative speed is the difference (|S₁ − S₂|).
</p

questions.question: 4 men and 3 women finish a job in 6 days, and 5 men and 7 women can do the same job in 4 days. How long will 8 men and 6 women take to do the same job?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The target workforce is 8 men and 6 women.

Notice that (8 men + 6 women) = 2 × (4 men + 3 women).

When the size of the workforce is exactly doubled, the time required to complete the job is halved.

Time taken = 6 days ÷ 2 = 3 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

4 Men and 3 Women complete the job in 6 days.

5 Men and 7 Women complete the job in 4 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of given days

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 4 Men + 3 Women
 6
 12
 12 ÷ 6 = 2
 
 

 5 Men + 7 Women
 4
 12 ÷ 4 = 3
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the efficiency of a Man be M and a Woman be W.

⇒ 4M + 3W = 2 ... (i)

⇒ 5M + 7W = 3 ... (ii)

⇒ Multiplying (i) by 5 and (ii) by 4 gives:

⇒ 20M + 15W = 10

⇒ 20M + 28W = 12

⇒ Subtracting the first from the second: 13W = 2 ⇒ W = 2/13

⇒ Substituting W in (i): 4M + 3 × (2/13) = 2

⇒ 4M = 2 − 6/13 = 20/13 ⇒ M = 5/13

⇒ Efficiency of target group (8M + 6W) = 8 × (5/13) + 6 × (2/13)

⇒ Target Efficiency = 40/13 + 12/13 = 52/13 = 4 units/day

⇒ Time taken = Total Work ÷ Efficiency = 12 ÷ 4 = 3 days

**∴ The correct answer is 3 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

MDH Concept

For group work problems, the relation M₁ × D₁ × H₁ ÷ W₁ = M₂ × D₂ × H₂ ÷ W₂ is universally used, where M is number of workers, D is days, H is hours, and W is work.

Work and Efficiency Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If the efficiency (or number of workers) is multiplied by a factor *k*, the time taken is directly divided by *k*.

Combined Efficiency

When multiple people or distinct groups work together, their one-day work (efficiencies) are added directly: Total Efficiency = E₁ + E₂ + ... + Eₙ.
</p

questions.question: Find the value of [ (63 div 9) times left{ (14)/(7) + (19)/(1) times (7 - 6) right} ]
A car covers four successive 8 km distances at speeds of 12 km/hr, 18 km/hr, 24 km/hr and 36 km/hr, respectively. Its average speed (in km/hr) over this distance is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For equal distances, assume the distance to be the LCM of the given speeds (12, 18, 24, 36) = 72 km.

Total time taken for 4 segments = (72 ÷ 12) + (72 ÷ 18) + (72 ÷ 24) + (72 ÷ 36) = 6 + 4 + 3 + 2 = 15 hours.

Total assumed distance = 4 × 72 = 288 km.

Average speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 288 ÷ 15 = 19.2 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 19.2 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Four equal successive distances = 8 km each

Speeds for each segment = 12 km/hr, 18 km/hr, 24 km/hr, and 36 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 
 
 
 

 8 km

 18 km/hr
 24 km/hr
 36 km/hr

 t₁ = 8/12 h
 t₂ = 8/18 h
 t₃ = 8/24 h
 t₄ = 8/36 h

 Total Distance = 32 km
 Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 8 + 8 + 8 + 8 = 32 km

⇒ Total Time = (8 ÷ 12) + (8 ÷ 18) + (8 ÷ 24) + (8 ÷ 36)

⇒ Total Time = 2/3 + 4/9 + 1/3 + 2/9

⇒ Total Time = (2/3 + 1/3) + (4/9 + 2/9)

⇒ Total Time = 1 + 6/9 = 1 + 2/3 = 5/3 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 32 ÷ (5/3)

⇒ Average Speed = (32 × 3) ÷ 5 = 96 ÷ 5

⇒ Average Speed = 19.2 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 19.2 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Concept of Average Speed

Average speed is always calculated as Total Distance ÷ Total Time. It is not the simple arithmetic mean of the given speeds unless the time traveled at each speed is exactly identical.

Average Speed for Two Equal Distances

If a person travels two equal halves of a journey at speeds x and y, the average speed is given directly by the formula: (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

If a person travels three equal parts of a journey at speeds x, y, and z, the average speed is calculated as: (3 × x × y × z) ÷ (xy + yz + zx).
</p

questions.question: The average age of 39 students of a class is 39 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 40 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:

By net deviation method: Value of new member = Old Average + (Total new members × Increase in average)

questions.question: If the radius of a hemisphere is 13√3 cm, find its curved surface area.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a hemisphere is calculated directly using the formula 2πr².

⇒ CSA = 2 × π × (13√3)²

⇒ CSA = 2 × π × 169 × 3 = 1014π cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 1014π cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• 
 r = 13√3 cm
 Curved Surface Area = 2πr²

**Given:**

Radius of the hemisphere (r) = 13√3 cm

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a hemisphere = 2πr²

**Calculation:**

⇒ CSA = 2 × π × (13√3)²

⇒ CSA = 2 × π × (13² × (√3)²)

⇒ CSA = 2 × π × (169 × 3)

⇒ CSA = 2 × π × 507

⇒ CSA = 1014π cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 1014π cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Hemisphere

The total surface area includes both the curved surface and the flat circular base. Formula: TSA = 3πr²

Volume of a Hemisphere

The volume represents the total 3D space occupied by the hemisphere. Formula: Volume = (2 ÷ 3)πr³

Surface Area & Volume of a Complete Sphere

For a full sphere of radius r, Surface Area = 4πr² and Volume = (4 ÷ 3)πr³
</p

questions.question: The price of fuel decreases by 40%, 50% and 15% in three successive months, but increases by 40% in the fourth month. What is the percentage increase/decrease in the price of fuel in the fourth month as compared to its original price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial price of the fuel be 100.

Using the successive percentage multiplying factor method:

Final price = 100 × (1 − 0.40) × (1 − 0.50) × (1 − 0.15) × (1 + 0.40)

Final price = 100 × 0.60 × 0.50 × 0.85 × 1.40 = 35.7

Percentage decrease = 100 − 35.7 = 64.3%

**∴ The correct answer is 64.3% decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Successive changes in fuel price: −40%, −50%, −15% and +40%.

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 ± R₁/100) × (1 ± R₂/100) × ...

 Net Decrease: 100 − 35.7 = 64.3%

**Calculations:**

Let the original price of the fuel be 100.

⇒ Price after 1st month = 100 × (100 − 40)/100 = 60

⇒ Price after 2ⁿd month = 60 × (100 − 50)/100 = 30

⇒ Price after 3rd month = 30 × (100 − 15)/100 = 25.5

⇒ Price after 4th month = 25.5 × (100 + 40)/100 = 35.7

⇒ Net decrease = Initial Price − Final Price = 100 − 35.7 = 64.3

Since the final value is lower than the initial value, there is an overall decrease of 64.3%.

**∴ The correct answer is 64.3% decrease.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Multiplying Factor Method

This method is the fastest technique for calculating multiple successive percentage changes. Simply multiply the base value by (1 ± r/100) for every consecutive change step involved.

Successive Percentage Change Formula

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the net percentage change can be directly found using the formula (a + b + (a × b)/100)%. Use positive signs for increases and negative signs for decreases.

Percentage Reversibility

A helpful trick to mentally solve complex percentages is that x% of y is exactly equal to y% of x. Applying this can often simplify fractions and calculations without altering the final result.
</p

questions.question: If the third proportional of 3x² and 4xy is 48, then the positive value of y is:

The third proportional of two terms a and b is calculated as b² ÷ a.

⇒ 48 = (4xy)² ÷ 3x²

⇒ 48 = 16x²y² ÷ 3x²

⇒ 48 = 16y² ÷ 3

Mean Proportional

questions.question: If at same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹40 and compound interest is ₹65, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
questions.solution:

questions.question: X is a greatest three-digit number exactly divisible by 12, 20, and 25. The sum of the digits of X is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The required number must be a multiple of the LCM of 12, 20, and 25.

LCM(12, 20, 25) = 300.

The greatest 3-digit multiple of 300 is simply 300 × 3 = 900.

The sum of the digits of 900 is 9 + 0 + 0 = 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The divisors are 12, 20, and 25.

X is the greatest 3-digit number perfectly divisible by these numbers.

**Concept Used:**

The smallest number exactly divisible by a set of numbers is their Lowest Common Multiple (LCM).

Any other number divisible by these numbers must be a multiple of their LCM.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 12 = 2² × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 20 = 2² × 5

⇒ Prime factorization of 25 = 5²

⇒ LCM of (12, 20, 25) = highest powers of prime factors = 2² × 3 × 5²

⇒ LCM = 4 × 3 × 25 = 300

⇒ The greatest 3-digit number is 999.

⇒ Dividing 999 by 300 gives a quotient of 3 and a remainder of 99.

⇒ The greatest 3-digit number exactly divisible by 300 is 999 − 99 = 900.

⇒ So, X = 900.

⇒ The sum of the digits of X = 9 + 0 + 0 = 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Lowest Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest non-zero number that is a multiple of two or more given numbers. It is found by multiplying the highest powers of all prime factors present.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The largest number that exactly divides two or more given numbers without leaving a remainder. It is calculated by taking the lowest powers of the common prime factors.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is exactly divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 9.

questions.question: If the selling price of five Bluetooth devices is ₹14,430 after allowing a discount of 26% on the marked price, then the marked price of one device is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling price of 1 device = 14430 ÷ 5 = ₹2,886

Value of SP is (100% − 26%) = 74% of the Marked Price.

MP = 2886 × (100 ÷ 74) = ₹3,900

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Selling price of 5 devices = ₹14,430

 Marked Price

SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Selling price of 1 device = 14430 ÷ 5 = ₹2,886

⇒ 2886 = MP × (100 − 26) ÷ 100

⇒ 2886 = MP × (74 ÷ 100)

⇒ MP = (2886 × 100) ÷ 74

⇒ MP = 39 × 100 = ₹3,900

Marked Price (MP) and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of an article. Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount amount.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the single equivalent discount percentage is given by: (a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100)%.

Relationship between CP and MP

The direct ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price can be determined by the formula: CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%).
